title: Endpoint on-ramp & version-pin copy sprint — wireframes + backlog
content:
Purpose:
This is a focused sprint note capturing wireframe sketches, microcopy experiments, and a lightweight backlog for the endpoint on-ramp and model-version pinning UX. Goal: reduce time-to-first-endpoint for new users, make pinning semantics discoverable, and provide clear fallback behavior copy for reliability scenarios.

Context & assumptions:
- Target persona: backend/frontend engineers and platform engineers who want a quick path from model browse -> endpoint -> smoke test.
- We ship a simple 'fast create' endpoint flow (defaults + smart suggestions) and an advanced flow (tunable batching, cache, runtime).
- Pinning should be safe: users need to know what pinned means (exact model+weights+quantization) and how rollbacks/fallbacks behave.

High-level outcomes we want to validate in this sprint:
1) Users can create a functional endpoint in < 3 minutes with minimal fields filled.
2) Pin modal explains tradeoffs in < 2 lines + optional 'learn more'.
3) Model catalog search -> endpoint button feels like one continuous flow.

Rough wireframe (ascii) — fast path:
[Model Catalog]  [search][filters]
  --------------------------------------
  | Model card                              |  [Create endpoint] (primary)
  | - name                                   |  [Preview weights] (secondary)
  | - top perf metric                         |
  --------------------------------------
-> click Create endpoint (fast) -> QuickCreate modal:
  [Quick endpoint name]  [region select]
  [Auth: api key toggle] [Traffic: default]
  [Create & Test] (primary) [Advanced options] (link)

QuickCreate copy draft (primary labels + microcopy):
- Modal title: Create endpoint from Model — fast path
- Endpoint name input placeholder: my-replies-endpoint
- Region select label: Region (auto-select based on org preference)
- Auth toggle: Allow API key (recommended for quick testing) — tooltip: Temporarily issues a test key valid for 24h
- Create & Test button: Create endpoint and run a test request
- Secondary link: Advanced options — go to detailed config

Pinning UX flow & wireframe:
- Context: from model detail or endpoint management -> Pin version (button on model card and version dropdown)
- Trigger: `Pin model version` opens a modal with compact summary

Pin modal copy drafts (short + long versions):
- Title options: 
  A) Pin version to endpoint
  B) Lock this model version
- Short description (2-line): 
  A) This pins the exact model build (weights, quantization, and config). Future catalog updates won’t change this endpoint.
  B) Lock to a model snapshot — safe, reproducible, and rollback-friendly.
- Callouts: 
  - Recommended for production endpoints.
  - Not recommended if you want automatic model upgrades.
- Buttons: 
  Primary: Pin version
  Secondary: Save as "latest" (alias) instead of pinning — tooltip: "Save as latest" keeps endpoint on the model family but may change behavior when we roll newer variants.

Microcopy variants for pinning tooltip (A/B):
- Variant A (explicit): Pin locks the exact artifact (weights + quantization). Use when you need deterministic outputs.
- Variant B (concise): Pin = reproducible outputs. Good for production.

Failure & fallback copy (for runtime degradations):
- Inline banner in endpoint settings when pinned model is not available: 
  Headline: Pinned model temporarily unavailable
  Body: Redwood will route to the nearest compatible model variant to keep traffic flowing. You can disable automatic fallback in Advanced -> Fallback policy.
  CTA: View fallback history

Observability & feedback microcopy:
- After create+test success toast: Endpoint created — 200 OK response from model.
- If test fails: Endpoint created (unhealthy) — See logs or retry test. Button: View logs

Accessibility notes:
- All modals must have explicit titles and aria-describedby linking to the short description.
- Primary action is focusable and keyboard-activatable.
- Pin modal must expose the model artifact id (read-only) and allow copy-to-clipboard with accessible aria-label.

Backlog / grooming items (ordered):
1) UX dev task: QuickCreate modal — implement defaults + region auto-select (2d) — JIRA:CR-5421
2) Eng task: Ensure endpoint create API returns artifact_id for pinned/non-pinned flows (backend) (3d) — JIRA:CR-5422
3) Copy task: Finalize pin modal short/long copy + tooltip variants A/B (1d) — owner: Maya
4) QA: Add smoke tests for Create & Test success and failure banners (1d)
5) Product: Decide fallback policy default for pinned endpoints (auto-route vs fail-fast) — meeting required (1h)

Open questions / risks:
- Should pinned endpoints default to auto-fallback to a compatible variant or fail traffic? (ops cost, customer expectations).
- How do we present quantization differences succinctly — users may not understand LO/INT8 terms. Need short explainer link.
- Do we offer a "pin preview" where we run a small diff between latest and pinned outputs during creation? (useful but expensive)

A/B experiment ideas (small scope):
- Test pin modal title: "Pin version" vs "Lock version" for downstream comprehension (measured by drop-off in pin confirmations).
- Test Create & Test CTA phrasing: "Create endpoint and run test" vs "Create and try it now" (engagement on first request).

Decisions to surface to engineering: 
- Default quick-create should enable short-lived API key for testing only (24h) unless org policy forbids it.
- Pin modal must include an explicit row showing: artifact_id, model_family, version_tag, runtime_profile (if quantized).

Next steps (this week):
- Maya: finalize copy variants and push to GH PR for console copy (due: 2025-11-13).
- Arjun: sketch hi-fi modal mockups in Figma and link them in Confluence.
- Lucia + Ben: confirm API contract for pin and fallback (sync Wed).

Notes to reviewers:
- Look for clarity and concision in the pin modal. Avoid heavy engineering jargon.
- If you think fallback should be opt-in (fail-fast by default), add a comment and reasoning.

Quick links:
- Draft figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/endpoint-onramp
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENDPOINT-ONRAMP-2025
- Backend API proto: github.com/redwood-inference/protos/endpoint.proto

Raw wireframe alt (compact checklist for devs):
- [ ] Model -> Create endpoint (fast modal)
- [ ] QuickCreate: name, region, test toggle, create & test
- [ ] Pin modal: short desc, artifact details, pin vs alias choices, fallback policy link
- [ ] Banners: created-ok, created-unhealthy, pinned-unavailable

-- end of sprint note --
